en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Rainy Season, 39. The Training Rule on the Rainy Season:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were wandering on tour during the rainy season.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs wander on tour during the rainy season, trampling green grass, harming one-sensed life, and bringing many small creatures to their destruction?”
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these bhikkhunīs go wandering on tour during the rains retreat?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunīs are wandering on tour during the rains retreat?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can bhikkhunīs go on a journey during the rains?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "‘If a bhikkhunī goes on a journey during the rains, she commits an offense of wrong-doing.’"
“Whatever nun, however, should go on a walking tour during the rains retreat, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"During the rains" means:
Having stayed during either the first three months or the last three months, he should go on a wandering tour.
"Should go on a wandering tour" means:
for every interval between villages within a range reachable by the flight of a cock, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
In a forest devoid of villages, for every half-yojana traveled, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense if one goes on account of a need lasting seven days.
If she goes because she has been harassed by someone,
in times of distress,
or if she is insane;
"By one who is a first offender":
thus ends the ninth training rule.
